title: In Photos: The Sea Creatures Lurking Off the Shores of Nantucket - Nautilus
gist: New England Aquarium aerial surveys of the Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument reveal abundant marine megafauna, contradicting the notion that the open ocean is a lifeless 'biological desert.'

themes.theme: Biological deserts of the open ocean

insights.claim: Marine biologists term vast swaths of open ocean 'biological deserts' because they lack the phytoplankton needed to anchor robust food webs like those around coral reefs and coastal estuaries.
insights.speaker: Bob Grant
insights.so_what: Establishes the baseline expectation the survey findings push back against.
insights.locator: marine biologists term some areas of Earth’s seas “biological deserts,”

insights.claim: The Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument spans more than 4,900 square miles about 130 miles southeast of Cape Cod and hosts underwater volcanoes and canyons teeming with sea life.
insights.speaker: Bob Grant
entities: Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument
insights.so_what: Documents the ecological value of a specific protected area, relevant to conservation policy.
insights.locator: This protected area, stretching more than 4,900 square miles

insights.claim: Aerial surveys shared by the New England Aquarium captured abundant marine megafauna—from deep-sea corals and seabirds to marine mammals and fish—in the monument's waters.
insights.speaker: Bob Grant
insights.so_what: Provides observational evidence of biodiversity concentrated around seamounts and canyons.
insights.locator: recently shared by the New England Aquarium

top_entities: Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument
